items.q: But, now, Buck Clayton is a poet. So, Djangó, and -- they all used to play together.

ctx.x: Or, if you are a poet, to a jazz man, either they make statements -- some of them babble, some of them are painters, some of them paint poetry, and are poets, see.

But, now, Buck Clayton is a poet. So, Djangó, and -- they all used to play together. All of them played together and when Oscar made something pretty, Djangó would -- hee, hee, hee, he had that little funny smile and Oscar would say, please -- wait a minute, then, right through that little drink of Pernot. At that time, pernot was a good -- was the drink --

items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: and we played a lot of things for him and Mezzrow was here then, Sidney Bechet Happy Caldwell, Jack Butler, a lot of them.

ctx.x: having trouble with his wife. She was putting him down. So we all saved up enough money and caught the Isle de France and went over there. But before we went Paradisio has been to New York, he came to New York somewhere down in that time.

And he told us he said if you ever get to France just let me know and I'll arrange something for you. And we always kept that in our minds you know, because we met him at the boat and we played a lot of things for him and Mezzrow was here then, Sidney Bechet Happy Caldwell, Jack Butler, a lot of them.
We all met him at the boat and we made him kind of happy to be in the States, it was his first trip. So he said, if you ever get to Europe and I was learning to speak French at that time,
